### About Me

<br>

I’m **Nicole Sanchez Flores**, an undergraduate at **[Smith College](https://www.smith.edu/)** majoring in **Statistics & Data Science and Psychology**. I’m passionate about using data to understand human behavior and improve real-world decision-making. I’ve developed experience in **R, Python, SQL, and statistical modeling** through projects in machine learning, health analytics, and social sciences.

I am from **Brooklyn, New York**, and I am especially proud to represent **first-generation Latine students** in academic and technical spaces.

<br>

### What I'm currently working on

I plan to pursue graduate study in **Applied Statistics** with a focus on psychology, health, and social impact.

Right now, I am working with **[Dr. Amanda Almond](https://www.citytech.cuny.edu/faculty/AAlmond)** to present research on **microaggressions and doctor–patient relationships** at the **[Eastern Psychological Association Conference](https://www.easternpsychological.org/i4a/pages/index.cfm?pageID=3501)**.

On campus, I am also:
- a **Peer Advisor** at the **[Lazarus Center for Career Development](https://www.smith.edu/about-smith/lazarus-center-career-development)**
- a **First Gen Outloud Intern** at **[Smith College](https://www.smith.edu/)**

<br>

### What drives me

I love research because it combines **human stories and data** where numbers can illuminate lived experiences, expose inequities, and support better policies in health and society. I’m excited by careers and research roles where I can contribute to **data-driven solutions that lift communities**. 

Check out some of my work [Projects]()
